fullarm:
Context from a materials paper:
- Visible-light photocatalytic H2 evolution on ZnIn2S4 needs faster separation of photogenerated carriers and more active surface sites
- Tuning the Ag:Pd ratio of an alloy cocatalyst sets an appropriate Schottky barrier height on ZIS and so maximises H2 evolution
- Deposit 0D metallic Ag-Pd alloy nanoparticles (1.0 wt%) on the ZIS surface as cocatalyst
- Chemical reduction of Ag+ and Pd2+ deposits Ag/Pd nanoparticles onto the ZIS microspheres
- Ag and Pd form an interacting alloy: electron density redistributes between Ag and Pd in Ag0.25Pd0.75-ZIS

Panels:
- F9a: caption: Fig. 8 ... Free energy profiles for hydrogen evolution reactions on Pd(111), Pd0.75Ag0.25(111) , Pd0.5Ag0.5(111) , Pd0.25Ag0.75 (111) and Ag(111)

Question: Panel F9a shows the computed hydrogen-adsorption free-energy diagram for pure Pd, pure Ag, and the three intermediate Pd-Ag alloy compositions deposited on ZIS. Reading directly from that panel, what free-energy value does each of the five surfaces show, and which one sits closest to zero?
